entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimant before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Pala in O.P.(M.V) No.666 of 2017, seeks to challenge the award dated 12.06.2020.
The accident occurred on 02.05.2014, when the claimant was aged 22 years.

2. Heard Sri. Manuel Kachiramattam, the learned counsel for the appellant, and Sri. A.C. Devy, the learned counsel for the respondent insurance company.
3.

The short issue arising for consideration in this appeal is regarding the fixation of the notional income by the Tribunal, with reference to Ext. A7 certificate, which evidenced a course completion by the claimant as an electrician, he claimed that he was earning a monthly income of Rs.15,000/.
However, the Tribunal in the impugned award fixed the monthly income at Rs.11,000/-.
4. A perusal of the award would show that on the basis of Ext.A7 certificate, referred to above, the fact that the 2025:KER:94563 claimant was an electrician has been accepted by the Tribunal.
However, the said certificate was not acted upon with reference to the claim for the notional income.
Prima facie, the finding of the Tribunal cannot be said to be incorrect or arbitrary.
5. At the same time, even though no evidence as regards the notional income was produced in the case at hand, the vocation of the claimant as an electrician is accepted by the Tribunal.
In such circumstances, notional income ought to have been fixed at least at Rs.11,500/-, since an electrician would definitely fetch a monthly income in that range.
Therefore, to that extent, the award of the Tribunal requires modification, and I do so.

6. Though Sri. Manuel Kachiramattam would make a submission with respect to the requirement to make enhancements under various other heads, a perusal of the award would show that more or less sufficient and reasonable compensation has been awarded by the Tribunal under the 2025:KER:94563 various other heads.
7. In such circumstances, the award of the Tribunal stands sustained subject to the modification of notional income as noticed above.

In the result, this appeal is partly allowed, modifying the impugned award, entitling the appellant to get an additional 2025:KER:94563 amount of Rs. 16,796/- (Rupees Sixteen Thousand Seven Hundred and Ninety Six only), along with the amounts already awarded by the Tribunal, to be paid by the respondent Insurance company.
Needless to say, all other findings and directions of the Tribunal in the impugned award, including the rate of interest, will remain unaltered.
